title: Phytochemical Profiling and Investigation of Analgesic, Anti-Diarrheal, and CNS Depressant Activity of Leea Macrophylla (Roxb.) Extract Using Experimental and Computational Approaches
content: Leea macrophylla is used in traditional medicine in Bangladesh, yet its whole plant has been little examined for analgesic, antidiarrheal and central nervous system (CNS) effects. A methanolic whole-plant extract (MELM) was profiled by gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS). Male Swiss albino mice received MELM (200, 400 and 600 mg/kg) in tail-flick, formalin-induced paw-licking and biting, castor oil-induced diarrhea and phenobarbitone-induced sleep tests. Identified compounds were docked to the μ-opioid receptor, cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), M3 muscarinic receptor and GABA_A receptor and screened by ADMET (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, toxicity) prediction. GC–MS identified 67 compounds, chiefly fatty acid derivatives and phytol. MELM increased tail-flick latency in a dose- and time-dependent manner and reduced formalin-induced licking and biting by up to 74.19% (600 mg/kg). Fecal output fell by 82.24% at 200 mg/kg, with weaker effects at higher doses. MELM shortened phenobarbitone-induced sleep, significantly at 200 and 400 mg/kg, which does not indicate CNS depression. Campesterol and lanosterol ranked among the top-scoring compounds for several targets and met all ADMET criteria. MELM shows analgesic activity in mice and these sterols warrant further experimental validation.
